title: Image-guided, Laser-based Fabrication of Vascular-derived Microfluidic Networks
protocol: Generate virtual masks using image processing software.
Open the 3D TIF image stack of mouse brain microvasculature.
Crop the image stack to fit a 450 µm x 450 µm x 1.5 mm window for the desired microfluidic network.
Draw a square around the desired region and click "Image" → "Crop".
Remove unnecessary slices in the z-direction by clicking "Image" → "Duplicate" and specifying the slice range.
Ensure the desired features fit within the field of view (x by y) and working distance (z) for a 20X water immersion objective.
Rotate the image stack so that features are aligned with the x-direction using "Image" → "Transform" → "Rotate".
Scale the cropped image stack to match the pixel size used on the confocal microscope, type in "2446" for "Width" under "Image" → "Adjust" → "Size".
Threshold/binarize the image stack by typing "Ctrl + Shift + T", deselect "Dark Background", and click "apply" → "ok".
Invert the lookup table using "Image" → "Lookup Tables" → "Invert LUT".
Fit the binarized features with quadrilaterals parallel to the x-direction using a custom algorithm.
Convert each individual plane in the TIF image stack to an RLS file and change the file extension of the RLS files to .OVL for use during degradation.
Open the microscope software and click "Start System."
Select the objective "W Plan-Apochromat 20x/1.0 DIC VIS-IR M27 75mm" in the "Maintain" tab.
Ensure that the laser line (514 nm Argon laser) is selected and on in the "Laser" window.
Set the "Mode" to "Channel Mode", set "Switch track every" to "Frame", and select "Track1".
Select only the Ch1 fluorescent detector, with a range of 516 to 735 nm; a main beam splitter (MBS) 458/514 filter on the visible light line.
Deselect the bright-field photomultiplier tube detector, "T-PMT".
Set the "Scan Mode" to "Frame", the "Frame Size" to "2884" in X and Y.
Set the "Line Step" to "1", the "Number Averaging" to "1", the "Averaging Mode" to "Line", the "Averaging Method" to "Mean".
Set the "Bit Depth" to "16 Bit", and the "Direction" to "<->" for bidirectional scanning.
Set the "Speed" as desired in the "Acquisition Mode" window.
Set "Corr X" and "Y" to "0.05".
Ensure that the "Scan Area" displays an "Image Size" of "531.2 µm x 531.2 µm".
Set a "Pixel Size" of "0.18" in the "Scan Area" window.
Set the "Zoom" to "0.8".
Select "Track1" as the Ch1 fluorescent detector in the "Channels" window.
Select laser line "514" with a percent power of "10.0".
Set a "Pinhole" of "1AU".
Set an initial "Gain (Master)" of "800".
Set a "Digital Offset" of "0".
Set a "Digital Gain" of "1".
Ensure that the laser line (790 nm 140 fs pulsed Ti:S laser) is selected and on in the "Laser" window.
Set "GDD Correction" to "4000".
Select no fluorescent detectors in the "Light Path" window.
Place a MBS 458/514/561/633 filter on the visible light line.
Place a MBS 760+ filter on the invisible light line.
Deselect the bright-field photomultiplier tube detector, "T-PMT".
Check that the correct objective is listed in the "Acquisition Mode" window.
Set the "Speed" to "3".
Select "Track1" as the T-PMT detector.
Choose the laser line "790".
Set the percent power of the laser line to "100.0".
Set the initial "Gain (Master)" to "800".
Set the "Digital Offset" to "0".
Set the "Digital Gain" to "1".
Zero the stage by clicking "set zero".
Mark the location by clicking "Mark".
In the "Time Series" window, set "Cycles" as "1".
In the "Time Series" window, set "Interval" as "0".
Check the "Start Bleaching after # scans" box and set it to a value of "0 of 1".
Select the "Different scan speed" with a value of "3".
Set the pixel dwell time to 8.96 µs/pixel.
Select the laser line section in the "Bleach" window.
Choose the 790 laser line and set its percent power to "100.0".
Leave all other boxes in the bleach window unselected.
Save the bleach settings in the "Bleach" window.
Save this configuration as "Channel Formation".
Set the percent power in the "Channels" window to "0.2".
Set the speed in the "Acquisition Mode" window to "8".
Click "Snap" in the upper left of the screen.
Check that the image size is "531.2 µm x 531.2 µm".
Verify that the pixel size is "0.18".
Ensure that the X and Y locations in the "Stage" window are zeroed.
Mark the position before opening the microscope macro.
Type "Alt+F8", click "Load", and select the correct version of the microscope macro.
Click "Run" to open the microscope macro from the "Macro Control" window.
Close the "Macro Control" window.
Provide an arbitrary "Base File Name" in the "Saving" tab of the microscope macro.
Select "Single File Output".
Choose a "Temporary File" folder.
Set "Open Temp Folder" location to "1".
Select "Single Temporary Image Folder".
Name the recipe in "Store/Apply Recipe" with "Recall Locations List" selected.
Click "Store" to initially create the recipe.
Ensure that the "Scan Configuration" matches the name given to the microscope software configuration set in step 2.3 in the "Acquisition" tab of the microscope macro.
Set the "No of Time Points within Block" to "1".
Set an "Interval" of "0".
Highlight "Marked Z - Top of the Z Stack" green.
Ensure that "Wait Delay" is highlighted green in the "Timing" tab of the microscope macro.
Set "Experiment Repetitions" to "1".
Set "Group Repetitions" to "1".
Set "Wait Interval Before Block at First Location Only" to "0".
Set the z-spacing, "dZ", to "1 µm" in the "Z List" tab of the microscope macro.
Set the "Number of Positions" to match the number of virtual masks to be used.
Click the "Create Z Stack" button to make the "Z List" appear in the dropdown "List of Locations".
Check that the number of locations and z-spacing are correct, with X and Y locations set to zero.
Select the "Bleach" box and ensure that "Config." matches the bleach settings name in the main microscope software screen.
Set "Wait Delay After Bleach" to "0", deselect "spot", and leave the "ROI" empty.
In the "Regions" window, click "Load" and select the .OVL file for the mask at the bottom of the z-stack being degraded.
Add 500 mL of DI H2O to a 1-L beaker.
Stir in 2.922 g of sodium chloride, 1.196 g of HEPES, and 7.5 mL of TEOA with a stir bar in a fume hood.
Adjust the pH to 8.3 with 1 N sodium hydroxide solution by adding dropwise.
Sterile filter the solution through a 0.2-µm vacuum filtration cup into a 500-mL autoclaved glass media bottle.
Aliquot and store the filtered solution at 4 °C.
Attach a ring of double-sided adhesive with backing to a specialized 60-mm Petri dish with a 20-mm hole cut out of the bottom.
Press out any air bubbles from between the Petri dish and the adhesive.
Bring synthesized 3.4 kDa PEGDA out of the -80 °C freezer and allow it to reach room temperature.
Turn on the white light source at least 15 min before photopolymerizing hydrogels.
Add 1 mL of HBS with TEOA to a foil-covered, 2-mL amber centrifuge tube.
Add 10 µL of 1 mM eosin Y disodium salt in DI H2O to the amber centrifuge tube.
Extract a small volume of 1-vinyl-2-pyrrolidinone (NVP) into a glass beaker with a Pasteur pipette.
Pipette 3.5 µL of NVP into the amber centrifuge tube containing HBS, TEOA, and eosin Y.
Add 10 mg of 3.4kDa PEGDA to a foil-covered, 2-mL amber centrifuge tube.
Add 0.2 mL of the HBS, TEOA, eosin Y, NVP solution for a 5% w/v PEGDA pre-polymer solution.
Vortex until the PEGDA is fully dissolved.
Adjust the intensity of the white light source to 95 mW using a power meter and detector wand.
Build a PDMS mold on a larger surface for ease of handling.
Place two 500 µm-thick PDMS spacers onto a PDMS surface to create defined hydrogel edges.
Include a 300-µm PDMS spacer in the surface of the hydrogel.
Pipette 60 μL of the 5% w/v PEGDA pre-polymer solution onto the PDMS mold carefully.
Center and place a TMPSA functionalized, 40-mm diameter, #1.5 glass coverslip on top of the solution.
Ensure that the coverslip rests on the 500-μm PDMS spacers.
Place the PDMS, PEGDA pre-polymer solution and coverslip the assembly under the white light source for 3 min.
Flow DI H2O between the mold and the coverslip to separate the hydrogel from the PDMS.
Rinse the hydrogel with DI H2O.
Dry the edges of the coverslip with lab tissue.
Adhere the coverslip to the prepared Petri dish using adhesive.
Gently remove air bubbles from between the adhesive and the glass.
Submerge the hydrogel in the Petri dish with DI H2O.
Select the objective "W Plan-Apochromat 20x/1.0 DIC VIS-IR M27 75mm" in the microscope's "Maintain" tab.
Ensure the necessary laser lines (514 nm Argon laser and 790 nm 140 fs pulsed Ti:S laser) are on and warmed up.
Fit the hydrogel and Petri dish on the stage insert and place it on the microscope stage.
Fill the Petri dish with at least 5 mL of DI H2O.
Center the hydrogel and well features by eye before lowering the water immersion objective into the DI H2O.
Switch to the "Hydrogel Visualization" configuration from step 2.2.
Click "Live" to turn the laser line on.
Bring the objective closer to the hydrogel until the eosin Y signal can be seen by the Ch1 fluorescent detector.
Increase percent power or open the pinhole temporarily for easier detection of the hydrogel.
Once focused, drop the percent power and close the pinhole back to 1AU to avoid oversaturation.
Mark the locations of the top and bottom of the hydrogel in the "Stage" window.
Mark the location of the bottom of the well in the "Stage" window.
Use the joystick to find the edge of a well.
Position the hydrogel at the right or left side of the screen, with the well on the opposite side.
Ensure the hydrogel fills no more than two thirds of the field of view.
Set the "Step Size" to 150 in the "Focus" window.
Click the down arrow next to the "Z-Position" box to drop focus by 150 µm into the hydrogel.
Repeat step if necessary for accurate detection and marking.
Zero the X and Y location in the "Stage" window.
Delete all other marked locations.
Mark only the inlet location.
Snap an image and draw a rectangular region for the inlet channel using the rectangle button in the "Regions" window.
Ensure part of the region extends out into the well to connect it to the vascular network.
Next to the ROI generated in the "Regions" window, select "Acquisition" and deselect "Bleach" and "Analysis".
Save the "Hydrogel Visualization" configuration, then deselect "Regions".
Change to the "Channel Formation" configuration.
In the "Channel Formation" configuration, select "Regions" again.
Select only "Regions" and "Z-Stack" in the configuration.
Click the "Center" button at the top and then the "Center" button above "Offset" to set the center of the z-stack as the current Z-position.
Set the number of "Slices" with an "Interval" of "1".
Check that "Speed" in the "Acquisition Mode" window is set to "3".
Set the "Percent Power" in the "Channels" window to "100".
Save the configuration and click the "Start Experiment" button.
Increase the "Gain (Master)" in the "Channels" window if the region in the field of view is black.
Decrease the "Gain (Master)" if the region is white.
Adjust the "Cycles" in the "Time Series" window to degrade the inlet multiple times.
Click "live" to ensure that the inlet was formed.
Load any .OVL file from the z-stack of virtual masks in the "Regions" window.
Click the arrow button to display ROIs in the field of view.
Click "Live" to initiate live scanning with the "Hydrogel Visualization" configuration.
Position the hydrogel using the joystick or the "Stage" window such that the inlet connects correctly within the vascular network.

Drop the plane of focus down 50 µm from the previous centered Z-location, or 200 µm from the surface of the hydrogel, using the "Step Size" in the "Focus" window and clicking the down arrow next to the "Z-Position" box.
Zero the X and Y locations in the "Stage" window.
Delete all other marked locations.
Mark only this location as the starting point for the microscope macro.
Snap an image in the "Hydrogel Visualization" configuration.
Delete and deselect "Regions".
Save the configuration.
Change to the "Channel Formation" configuration.
Select only the "Time Series" and "Bleaching" windows.
Verify settings for the "Time Series" window as initially set.
Verify settings for the "Bleaching" window as initially set.
Set the "Speed" in the "Acquisition Mode" window to "8".
Set percent power of the laser line to "0.2" in the "Channels" window.
Save the configuration.
Open the microscope macro following step 3.5.
Select the previously made recipe from step 3 on the "Saving" tab.
Click "Apply" without clicking "Store".
Check settings on all tabs and verify virtual masks (.OVL files) are correctly associated with Z-locations in dropdown list.
Verify first Z-location matches marked location in the "Stage" window of the microscope software.
Save the "Channel Formation" configuration again.
Click "Update" in the microscope macro.
Click "No" to "Overwrite Current Location List?".
Click "Start" in the microscope macro to begin the recipe.
Close the microscope macro.
Switch to the "Hydrogel Visualization" configuration.
Use a lower laser power for imaging fluorescein (FITC)-labeled dextran.
Wick water from the well in the hydrogel using lab tissue.
Pipette 10 μL of 5 mg/mL 2,000 kDa FITC-labeled dextran in DI H2O into the well.
Use an incubated stage with 60% humidity or higher for imaging longer than 30 min.
Remove the hydrogel and Petri dish from the stage.
Mark the Petri dish to locate the formed vascular network.
